summary: No. Logistic Regression achieves higher stratified 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.9053) than Random Forest (0.9016) on the Adult Income dataset, with an average difference of 0.3232 percentage points favoring LogReg. This finding was validated across 5 repeated CV runs with different random seeds, and held consistently in 100% of validation runs.
methodological_choices: Target encoding: binary classification (income >50K vs <=50K). Preprocessing: missing values in categorical features imputed with mode, numerical features imputed with median. Feature engineering: categorical features one-hot encoded, numerical features standardized via StandardScaler. Models: scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier() and LogisticRegression() with default hyperparameters (RF: 100 trees; LR: lbfgs solver, max_iter=1000). Validation: stratified 5-fold cross-validation to preserve class balance. Evaluation metric: ROC-AUC (area under receiver operating characteristic curve) computed via cross_val_score. No class weighting or stratification-aware model adjustments beyond CV stratification.
verification_method: Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (5 independent runs with random seeds 42, 123, 456, 789, 999) to assess consistency across different fold partitions. For each seed, computed mean ROC-AUC and difference for both models.
verification_result: Highly stable. Logistic Regression outperformed Random Forest in all 5 repeated CV runs. Mean ROC-AUC across repeats: LR = 0.9053 (±0.0001), RF = 0.9020 (±0.0007). All individual differences (RF - LR) were negative: range [-0.0043, -0.0024]. The finding is not only confirmed but remarkably consistent across random partitions, indicating a genuine and robust difference in model performance on this dataset.
